exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 Visiting the Science Museum
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mia: Have you ever been to the new science museum, Leo?
Leo: Not yet. I've heard a robot has been built there that can talk.
Mia: Yes, it's amazing. It answers your questions about space and stars.
Leo: That sounds great. What else can we see?
Mia: There's a model of an electric car that has been designed by students.
Leo: Wow. I'd love to know how it works.
Mia: Then let's go this Saturday. Tickets have already been booked for us.
Leo: Perfect. I can't wait to learn something new!
exercises.translation_cn: 米娅问利奥去没去新科技馆;利奥没去,听说那里造了会说话的机器人;它能回答关于太空和星星的问题;还有学生设计的电动车模型;两人决定周六去,门票已经订好了。

questions.stem: Where are Mia and Leo talking about going?
What can the talking robot do?
options: Answer questions about space and stars.

questions.stem: Who designed the electric car model?
When will they go to the museum?
What has already been done for them?

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 The Four Great Inventions
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Ancient China is famous for four great inventions.
They are gunpowder, papermaking, printing and the compass.
Each of these inventions has changed the world in a deep way.
Thanks to the compass, sailors could travel far across the sea.
Even today, these old ideas are still used in modern life.
exercises.translation_cn: 古代中国以四大发明闻名:火药、造纸、印刷和指南针;每一项都深刻改变了世界;有了指南针,水手能远渡重洋;直到今天,这些古老的智慧仍用于现代生活。

questions.stem: How many great inventions is ancient China famous for?
Which of these is one of the four inventions?
What did each invention do to the world?
How did the compass help sailors?
options: They could fly to the Moon.
They could travel far across the sea.

questions.stem: Are these old ideas still useful today?

exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 Acting Out the Telephone Story
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Anna: Let's practise the conversation about how the telephone was invented.
Ben: Good idea. You ask the questions, and I'll be the expert.
Anna: So, who was the telephone invented by?
Ben: It was invented by Alexander Graham Bell in 1876.
Anna: What gave him the idea?
Ben: His mother could not hear well, so he became interested in sound.
Anna: And what was the first phone call about?
Ben: He simply called his helper in the next room to test the machine.
exercises.translation_cn: 安娜和本排练关于电话发明的对话;安娜提问,本扮专家;电话由亚历山大·格雷厄姆·贝尔于1876年发明;因母亲听力不好,他对声音产生兴趣;第一通电话只是叫隔壁房间的助手来测试机器。

questions.stem: What are Anna and Ben practising?
options: A conversation about the telephone's invention.

questions.stem: Who was the telephone invented by?
In which year was it invented?
Why did Bell become interested in sound?
options: His mother could not hear well.

questions.stem: What was the first phone call about?
options: Testing the machine with his helper.

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 Printing Body Parts
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Scientists have found an amazing new use for 3D printers.
These machines can now make parts of the human body.
A patient once received a new ear that had been printed in a lab.
Because each part is made to fit one person, operations become safer.
In the future, fewer sick people may have to wait for help.
exercises.translation_cn: 科学家为3D打印机找到惊人新用途:这些机器如今能制造人体部件;曾有病人获得一只在实验室打印出的新耳朵;由于每个部件都为一个人量身打印,手术更安全;未来,需要等待救治的病人也许会更少。

questions.stem: What new use have scientists found for 3D printers?
options: Making parts of the human body.

questions.stem: What did one patient receive?
Why are these operations safer?
options: The parts are made of paper.
Each part fits one person exactly.

questions.stem: What may happen in the future?
options: Fewer patients may have to wait.

questions.stem: Where was the new part printed?

exercises.title: U3 听力·对话 Choosing a Science Career
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Teacher: Have you decided what kind of scientist you want to be, Grace?
Grace: I think I'd like to be an astronomer and study the stars.
Teacher: That's wonderful. And what about you, Sam?
Sam: I'm more interested in living things, so maybe a biologist.
Teacher: Both are excellent choices. Science needs curious minds.
Grace: But the maths looks really hard.
Teacher: Don't worry. With patience, every difficult subject can be learned.
Sam: Then we'll both keep trying!
exercises.translation_cn: 老师问格蕾丝想当哪种科学家;格蕾丝想当天文学家研究星星;山姆对生物更感兴趣,想当生物学家;老师说两者都很好,科学需要好奇心;格蕾丝担心数学太难;老师鼓励说只要有耐心,再难的科目也能学会;两人决定继续努力。

questions.stem: What does Grace want to be?
What is Sam more interested in?
What does the teacher say science needs?
What is Grace worried about?
What does the teacher say about difficult subjects?
options: They can be learned with patience.

exercises.title: U3 听力·短文 Where Inventions Begin
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here is a simple truth about invention.
Most new ideas begin with a problem that needs a solution.
When something annoys us, we start to ask how it could be better.
That small question is often the first step of a great invention.
So never stop being curious, because every question may change the world.
exercises.translation_cn: 关于发明有个简单的道理:大多数新点子始于一个需要解决的问题;当某件事让我们烦恼时,我们便开始思考如何让它变得更好;那个小小的问题,往往是伟大发明的第一步;所以永远别停止好奇,因为每个问题都可能改变世界。

questions.stem: Where do most new ideas begin?
options: With a problem that needs solving.

questions.stem: What do we do when something annoys us?
options: We ask how it could be better.

questions.stem: What is often the first step of a great invention?
What should we never stop being?
Why is curiosity important?
options: Every question may change the world.
